text:
maria: Heads up — saw 5 KV-cache OOMs on hosted-prod over the last 24h, all with very long contexts (>30k tokens). Stack traces point at kv-page walker + large resident slab growth. attaching basic repro summary

liam: can you drop the perf profile and an example request id?

maria: repro id: req_2026_393210; sample prefix length 32768 tokens. profile: CPU flame shows lots of time in kv::evict_scan and in kernel selection path when sequence len > 2048. mem histogram attached:
```
# alloc histogram (approx)
kv_slab: 2.1GB
kv_pages: 6.8GB
model_kv_cache: 9.0GB
other: 1.2GB
```

phil: hmm - we shipped kernel heuristic change 6 days ago (commit 4f2b9c) that prefers grouped attention kernels for long sequences. Those kernels allocate larger contiguous page chunks for KV (faster perf avg) — maybe fragmentation+growth interact badly.

samir: also saw a spike in batch size around same time — batching heuristics were relaxed to favor throughput for small requests. Could be larger batches + longctx increasing kv footprint per worker.

maria: timeline aligns. OOMs only on nodes serving mixed small+very-long requests. Short sessions unaffected.

liam: low-effort immediate mitigation: introduce proxy-level backpressure rule: if prefix_token_count > 8k, route to a 'longctx-slim' variant (quantized, smaller-kv footprint) or reject with 429. Also enable aggressive kv-evict threshold on those sessions (evict when usage > 0.55 of slab).

phil: agree. we can wire a per-request flag for kernel selection fallback too: prefer compact kernels that are KV-friendly even if slightly slower. I'll sketch a patch.

alice-oncall: I'll roll a canary for the proxy routing rule now. planning: 5% traffic with threshold=8192 and fallback model m14-compact.

runtime-bot: deploy-started: rollout/proxy-backpressure-canary by alice-oncall at 2026-03-18T16:12:00Z

ci-bot: canary passed basic smoke 15m ago; no errors in canary pool.

samir: for medium-term: let's add a KV-allocator telemetry that reports fragmentation ratio (free_contiguous_bytes / total_free_bytes) per worker and a per-prefix kv-reservoir estimator so we can pre-check allocation before accepting request.

liam: also want a graceful-degrade path: if reservation fails, try auto-trim oldest prefixes (LRU eviction) up to X tokens, then fallback to model-variant. avoid hard OOM.

maria: noted. I ran a local repro with a patched kernel-selection flag: when forcing 'compact-kernel' we saw a 30% drop in peak kv-resident, and latency +8% p95. tradeoff seems acceptable for long contexts.

phil: patch diff for compact kernel flag (WIP):
```
- kernel_selector::prefer_grouped = true
+ kernel_selector::prefer_grouped = (ctx_len < 2048)
```

samir: good. for batching heuristics: add soft-batch-split on prefix length. i.e. if a batch mixes >1 request with prefix_len>8k, split into separate micro-batches. avoids multiplicative kv growth.

liam: +1. that should reduce cross-request kv amplification.

alice-oncall: canary finished. applying to 30% now with observability hooks on kv-resident, frag_ratio, evict_rate. will pause at any uptick >3x OOM rate.

runtime-bot: deploy-success: rollout/proxy-backpressure at 2026-03-18T16:47:20Z -> 30%

maria: after 2h telemetry: OOMs dropped from 5->1 in affected pool. got one residual OOM where prefix_len was 60k tokens and client used streaming append, caused hidden kv-growth.

samir: we should add a hard cap for streaming append total-prefix per session; for extremely long flows recommend chunking or external state.

phil: action items:
- PHIL: push compact-kernel conditional and a flag for per-request kernel override (PR#4123)
- SAMIR: implement soft-batch-split + frag telemetry (ticket INF-827)
- MARIA: add per-request reservation/early-reject and tune proxy thresholds (ticket INF-829)
- ALICE-ONCALL: monitor canary -> 100% if stable and roll back if OOMs spike

liam: for postmortem, capture a short perf appendix showing how kernel selection + batching heuristics interacted to amplify kv allocations. include the flame graphs and the before/after of compact-kernel test.

maria: will compile that and drop it in the incident doc. thanks all :eyes: 

alice-oncall: closing loop — alert rule added: KV_RESIDENT_PER_WORKER > 11GB for 2m -> page oncall. also added frag_ratio heatmap to runtime console.

runtime-bot: incident-note: mitigations applied, monitoring added.
